verdict.rationale: Claude Code's overview docs name all four tasks as things it handles: writing tests for untested code, fixing lint errors across a project, resolving merge conflicts, and updating dependencies. Supporting docs say it runs tests within its workflow and can run lint through hooks. Community complaints about general output quality are not specific to these tasks, so they do not create a dispute. missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs for each task (beyond one overview line), and independent or hands-on corroboration of test writing, lint fixing, merge-conflict resolution and dependency updates.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent write tests, fix lint errors, resolve merge conflicts, and update dependencies for me

citations.quote: Claude Code handles the tedious tasks that eat up your day: writing tests for untested code, fixing lint errors across a project, resolving merge conflicts, updating dependencies, and writing release notes.
reading issues, writing code, running tests, and submitting PRs—all from your terminal
Hooks let you run shell commands before or after Claude Code actions, like auto-formatting after every file edit or running lint before a commit.
